excerpts.text: Husband‘s family is very overwhelming and toxic. Mother-in-law was okay but also awful. I really don’t want to drive eight hours with toxic sister-in-law and husband and his father who has dementia, (who I look after as husband works full-time and of course as

I'd go as a support to your husband. Whatever you think of MIL, it'll be a difficult day for him and I can't imagine not being by my husbands side. You aren't there to remember MIL, you're there to support DH. How would you feel if the roles were reversed?
Would you not go to support your husband? If I was travelling that distance I would attend the service.
You go for your husband, OP. If he wants you there with him, you go. I think for a couple of hours you can put your own feelings to one side and concentrate on him.

Me again, sorry. I also think that husband and sister-in-law need to renegotiate their relationship as it’s now changed. The sister-in-law used to triangulate with the mother and it got really peculiar. It always felt like a game that we were losing, but we ne

I couldn’t be in a spa whilst my husband was at his mums funeral, regardless of their relationship? Sometimes we have to put our own feelings to one side to support our partners. Nobody wants to go to a funeral, toxic family or not.
The dynamics here sound very hard. I would attend to support your DH. I do understand though that it will be hard.
You want to sit in a spa whilst your DH attends his mother’s funeral? Are you always self centred or just when it comes to the important stuff?
